transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Um… I guess the main thing is that at work, on the floor, I’m having a hard time keeping my train of thought. I’m a nurse, and it feels like any little interruption—an IV pump beeping, a call light, someone asking another nurse something—can completely throw me off, and then I’m standing there trying to remember what patient flow issue I was even working on.

I don’t want to make it sound like I’m not capable or anything, because I do care a lot and I try really hard, but it’s been happening enough that I thought I should probably talk to someone about it.
When did you first start noticing this trouble staying focused—has it been going on since childhood, or did it start more recently, like in the past few weeks or months?

I think it goes back pretty far, honestly. I mean, I did well in school, so it was easy to kind of write it off, but even in elementary school my teachers would say I was bright, just… careless. Like I’d lose worksheets or forget to turn in homework that I had actually done.

My mom had to sit with me most nights to keep me on track, which I guess I always thought was normal at the time. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Aside from the distractibility, have you noticed yourself feeling persistently worried, on edge, or anxious throughout most days recently?

Um… I don’t think so, not in a constant way. I mean, I get stressed, like anyone would with work and everything, but I wouldn’t say I’m walking around anxious or on edge most of the day.

At least, I don’t think that’s the main thing. It feels more like I’m just trying to keep up and not miss things, if that makes sense.
